newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end down amid late T-bond sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end down amid late T-bond sales.

text.p: U.S. debt futures were mostly lower at the end of pit trading Thursday on heavy late selling after a largely technically driven day of light activity.

December U.S. 30-year Treasury bond futures fell on the close when a big dealer offered 700 to 800 contracts at roughly 115-19/32, which drew another major sale of 2,000 contracts by a large dealer, one pit trader said.
"That kind of put a lid on it," the trader said.
For most of the day, December T-bonds bounced between a major Fibonacci technical resistance level of 115-29/32 and support at about 115-19/32, traders said.

T-bond futures shortly after the opening hit a new nine-month high, the key resistance level of 115-29/32. Three midday runs at the high failed to breach it. One trader said volumes were too light to support sustainable gains.

The early high came on U.S. jobless claims data, which were at 344,000 for the week ended November 16, versus estimates for a slight rise to 332,000 and against the previous week's downward-revised 327,000.
The market sold off from the T-bond high on technical factors and the Philadephia Federal Reserve's November business outlook survey, traders said.
